security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 32 static findings. Markdown backtick alerts, generic anti-pattern headings, and the .env.example setup command are false positives; the three Python scripts retain medium filesystem risk because --output can overwrite caller-selected paths. No prompt injection, network access, credential exfiltration, or additional semantic abuse evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted report output paths in bundled Python scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve --output under a dedicated reports directory, refuse path traversal, and require explicit overwrite confirmation.

remediation.issue: Setup and deployment command examples may be copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: Add short safety notes before install, Docker, Kubernetes, and environment-file commands requiring explicit user approval.

content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss design risks, test scope, and implementation gaps. This skill provides structured threat modeling, audit checklists, pentest planning, and crypto guidance for authorized work.
actual_capabilities: Validates that a supplied target path exists before local script runs.
Generates simple status reports from the included Python tools.
Provides checklists for threat modeling, security auditing, and pentest planning.
Links to bundled reference guides for architecture, penetration testing, and cryptography.
Documents common development, analysis, and deployment command examples.
limitations: The included scripts are scaffolds and do not perform deep vulnerability scanning.
It does not verify authorization for penetration testing targets.
Command examples can modify local files or infrastructure if run without review.
Reference files contain generic guidance and need project-specific tailoring.

use_cases.title: Prepare an application security review
use_cases.description: Map review scope, identify likely control areas, and organize findings for an application before release.

use_cases.title: Plan authorized penetration testing
use_cases.description: Define target boundaries, expected outputs, and documentation needs before starting an approved assessment.

use_cases.title: Check implementation decisions
use_cases.description: Compare authentication, authorization, input handling, and cryptography choices against common security practices.

prompt_templates.title: Start a security review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project at a high level. Identify security areas to inspect first, expected evidence, and safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a threat model
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured analysis for a feature or service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a threat model for this feature. Cover assets, trust boundaries, entry points, abuse cases, and prioritized mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit architecture controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of design and implementation choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this architecture for authentication, authorization, data protection, logging, dependency, and deployment risks. Separate findings by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an authorized assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for approved penetration testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized penetration test for this scope. Include rules of engagement, test phases, evidence handling, risks, and remediation reporting.

output_examples.input: Review a new payments API before launch.
output_examples.output: The review highlights authentication gaps, sensitive data handling, audit logging, dependency risk, and launch-blocking checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a threat model for a customer file upload service.
output: Assets include uploaded files, customer identity, metadata, storage credentials, and processing logs.
Primary risks include malicious files, unauthorized access, excessive retention, and weak scan failure handling.
Recommended mitigations include scoped storage access, content validation, malware scanning, quarantine flows, and audit trails.

output_examples.input: Plan a scoped assessment for an internal admin portal.
output_examples.output: The plan defines approved targets, excluded systems, test windows, evidence rules, account handling, escalation paths, and report sections.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before any penetration testing workflow.
Review generated commands before running them, especially install, environment, Docker, and Kubernetes commands.
Treat script output as a starting point and validate findings with project-specific evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not run testing against systems outside the approved scope.
Do not treat the scaffold scripts as a complete vulnerability scanner.
Do not copy setup or deployment commands into production without review.

faq.question: Does this skill perform real vulnerability scanning?
faq.answer: No. The included scripts generate simple scaffold reports and need additional security tooling for deep scanning.

faq.question: Can I use it for penetration testing?
faq.answer: Use it only for planning and documentation of authorized assessments within a clearly approved scope.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence of network requests was found in the reviewed files.

faq.question: Why are filesystem risks listed?
faq.answer: Each Python script can write a JSON report to a caller-selected output path.

faq.question: What should I review before running commands?
faq.answer: Check paths, target scope, install commands, environment file changes, Docker actions, and Kubernetes actions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
